papers.markingGuideNote: Use the published scale where printed. Other placements allow 2 for a partially correct element. Deduct 3 for a mathematical error, or 1 for a slip or minor misreading; do not deduct an error twice. Specific table/edge deduction rules and algorithm-naming exceptions take precedence. Alternative valid methods are accepted.
papers.boundaryReview: Q2(b) has four shared component/collision placements plus a separate 5 for each final velocity: 25 for P including shared steps, 5 for Q. Q5(a)(i) diagrams receive 5 each. Q8(iii) velocities receive 5 each. Q6(i) and Q10(a)(i) pairs of recurrence values each share one 5. Q9(i) is one 10-mark table with a deduction of 1 per incorrect entry, not twelve one-mark tasks. Q9(ii) early and late times share a 20-mark scale. Q7(a)(i) keeps algorithm naming and construction together under its published 15-mark scale and naming exception. Required method steps are not split into independent cards.

papers.markingGuideNote: Use the published scale where printed. Other placements allow 2 for a partially correct element. Deduct 3 for a mathematical error, or 1 for a slip or minor misreading; do not deduct an error twice. Specific table/edge deduction rules and algorithm-naming exceptions take precedence. Alternative valid methods are accepted.
papers.boundaryReview: Q1(b)(i) the two masses share a single 5. Q3(iii) magnitudes and Q3(iv) angles receive 5 each. Q3(vii) both final constants share one 5 after the equations. Q6(v) the car and cyclist graphs receive 5 each. Q7(i) each velocity has a separate 5; two shared equation placements attach to S1 (15), with S2 separately worth 5. Q9(b)(i) force diagrams receive 5 each. Paired roots and paired projectile times share a final placement. Q4(a)(i) is a 10-mark network with one-mark deductions per edge. Choice plus justification in Q5(b) and Q10(v) remain single explained answers; they are not independent alternate answer routes.
